newsitem.title: UK: Mideast VLCCs stay soft on ample tonnage.
newsitem.headline: Mideast VLCCs stay soft on ample tonnage.

text.p: Middle East very large crude carrier (VLCC) rates remained soft on Friday on low enquiry and an over-supply of tonnage, brokers said.

VLCCs on westward voyages dipped below the W50 level, with 270,000 tonnes Mideast/Rotterdam and Mideast/U.S. Gulf put at W47.5, while to Singapore the 1975-built Berge Odel fetched just W46.5 for Sietco.
Brokers Galbraith's Ltd said the April 1996 pattern was being repeated and this implied that "further erosion will occur before the market bottoms out."

Galbraith's figures showed that Mideast/Japan rates, currently averaging W53.75, were well below the same week last year when they fetched W60, although Mideast/Red Sea rates were still well above a year ago (W49.75 versus W40).
Mideast/UKC rates are currently around W50, against W47.5 last year.

E.A. Gibson said in their weekly tanker report that Mideast/east liftings far outnumbered voyages west this week and that out of 16 vessels totalling four million tonnes, 12 went east, amounting to three million tonnes.

"Current availability indicates some 55 vessels of 16.5 million tonnes being ready between now and this time next month and, out of this total, 40 are VLCCs of which 18 can be classed as modern," they added.
But brokers said modern ships were not attracting much of a premium at present due to a surfeit of tonnage.
They also noted strong demand for VLCCs from West Africa, even though there had been little change in rates, with liftings to Asia on the increase.
Gibson said of 10 VLCCs fixed from West Africa, totalling 2.5 million tonnes, six were sailing east and four west.

They said that few VLCCs were fixed from West Africa until recently, but in 1996 they amounted to a sizeable 16 percent of the total, while there had also been an increase in fixing of VLCCs from the Mediterranean and North Sea.
But despite good demand for VLCCs from West Africa, rates showed a softer tone to the U.S. Gulf on Friday, dipping to W67.5.

Million-barrel ships from West Africa also had little difficulty in finding employment, with two going east and 10 west, Gibson said. Rates were fairly steady at around W90/95, with modern ships at the higher end of the scale.
The million-barrel market in the Med also held up around W95 with good demand for Iraqi crude from the Turkish port of Ceyhan, with similar rates achieved in northwest Europe.
Brokers said the 80,000 tonne (Aframax) North Sea market suffered from the good demand for VLCCs, with rates languishing around the W100 level or even lower.
But in the Med Aframax rates remained healthy at about W125, and up to W135 for a modern vessel.
Caribs/upcoast 70,000 tonne crude rates remained strong at W225, some 70 points above the average for last year, according to New York-based Rigos Chartering Inc.

However, Galbraith's said, "many feel that owners are holding onto the last few threads and a meltdown is about to occur," and added that a pointer in this direction could be the fixing of 50,000 tonnes of fuel oil as low as W150 to USAC. Caribs fuel oil was fixed at around W175 on Thursday.
The European fuel oil tanker market was quiet, with 25,000 tonnes inter-U.K./cont unchanged at W180 and cross-Med dipping to W185 from W195, brokers said.
--Michael Rank, London newsroom +44 171 542 4088
